problem: Rounded to two decimal places, what is the acute angle between the vectors  $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality and the Angle Between Two Vectors

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Acute Angle Between Two Vectors

examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula

$$
\cos\theta = \dfrac{\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{w}}{\Vert\mathbf{v}\Vert \, \Vert \mathbf{w}\Vert},
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{25}\cdot \sqrt{16}} \\  & =\frac{10}{5\cdot 4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta=\arccos \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}.
$$

feedback.problem: Given that $‖u‖=5$ and $u\cdot v=-15$, find the smallest possible value of $‖v‖.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-15| & \le 5\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 15 & \le 5\cdot ‖v‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $\frac{1}{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}\cdot 15 & \le \frac{1}{5}\cdot 5\cdot ‖v‖ \\ 3 & \le ‖v‖\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $‖v‖$
is  $3.$
